sermon.title: The Acceptable Other Harvest 11/19/2017
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that God has more after salvation for the untaught “other harvest”: the baptism of power, his glory, the divine nature, knowing God as Job did, and wisdom from above. He warns that many, like Israel at Sinai and the disciples who left in John 6, refuse to draw near, and urges believers to be like the Bereans who searched the scriptures daily.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: The pastor’s wife is named in the transcript only. Points to check: Job “2,000 years before Christ”; Thessalonian Jews traveled “50 miles” to Berea; “Exodus 1917” as spoken (Exodus 19:17). Sensitive content kept as spoken: those who say tongues are the devil “just full of baloney”; “waiting for the rapture and all that nonsense”; Christian radio, TV, bookstores and music repeating “lies ... deception”; believers who reject knowing Jesus; Thessalonian Jews “so adamant and hard-headed and one-sided”.

scriptures.text_nkjv: As the living Father sent Me, and I live because of the Father, so he who feeds on Me will live because of Me.
Therefore many of His disciples, when they heard this, said, “This is a hard saying; who can understand it?”
From that time many of His disciples went back and walked with Him no more.

scriptures.text_nkjv: These were more fair-minded than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness, and searched the Scriptures daily to find out whether these things were so.
But when the Jews from Thessalonica learned that the word of God was preached by Paul at Berea, they came there also and stirred up the crowds.

faqs.question: Did God fill people who didn’t yet believe in Jesus?
faqs.answer: Yes, he says—Cornelius and the Ephesians.

faqs.question: To whom is the promise?
faqs.answer: You, your children, those afar off.
